hooks.text: A secret radioactive clock is bolted to the side of Voyager.
NASA electroplated pure uranium-238 onto the covers of the Voyager records.
A billion-year time capsule carries a hidden atomic clock on its cover.

title: The Radioactive Clock Hiding on Voyager
description: The Voyager Golden Record carries a hidden atomic clock made of uranium-238 to tell aliens how old it is.

beats.text: A secret radioactive clock is bolted to the side of Voyager.
beats.visual: artist concept of Voyager 1 spacecraft in interstellar space, NASA, 1977

beats.text: In 1977, two robotic spacecraft launched into the great void carrying golden phonograph records designed to tell Earth's complete story to the stars.
beats.visual: photograph of Voyager Golden Record cover diagram, NASA, 1977

beats.text: Inside are spoken greetings in 55 different human languages, whale songs, and human brainwaves recorded during a deeply emotional moment of falling in love.
beats.visual: portrait of Carl Sagan and Ann Druyan, NASA, 1977

beats.text: But the protective aluminum cover itself holds an ultra-pure sample of heavy uranium-238.
beats.visual: photograph of uranium element sample, periodic table

beats.text: Because this exact isotope decays with a half-life of approximately 4.5 billion years, any finder can calculate the exact time since launch.
That brilliant atomic clock is built right into the side of Voyager.
beats.visual: artist concept of Voyager spacecraft cruising past Jupiter, NASA, 1979
